history.summary: Stored SMTP secrets can be redirected to client-controlled connection fields; MySQL storage bounds can truncate rollback data.
Bound preserved credentials to stored routing context and added storage-safe byte limits with transactional readback verification, including non-strict MySQL coverage.
Both security fixes verified complete and correct. Context binding prevents credential redirect. Storage verification prevents truncation data loss. All goal criteria remain met.
Independent specialist re-review confirmed both original findings closed with no remaining high-confidence security issue.
SQLite Down can reuse deleted IDs, stored-password test email discards safe unsaved fields, and MySQL no-op PUT can falsely fail.
Preserved SQLite SMTP ID history, separated protected test-email routing from safe message fields, and verified MySQL no-op updates in transaction.

All three profile-integrity corrections verified complete and transactional. SQLite sequence preserved after delete. Test-email binds protected auth/routing while retaining safe from/headers. MySQL no-op PUT verifies all fields match before committing. All goal criteria remain met.
Final re-review confirmed all three correctness findings closed with no regression.
Final security review found no remaining high-confidence exploit or data-loss issue.
Frontend browser smoke failed twice because the settings retry contract observed four unexpected prior success flash events.
Made the successful-controls browser scenario await its flash callback before the failure/retry scenario resets event state.

Flash-event race condition fixed correctly. Asynchronous success callback now awaited before test state reset, eliminating timing-dependent race on slow CI workers. Only test code changed; no product code, assertions, timeouts, or SMTP contract regressions. All 70+ goal criteria remain met.
